Apple today updated its vintage and obsolete products list, with the iPhone X and the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro now classified as obsolete. Here's what this classification means.

iPhone X and 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro now listed as obsolete

Apple today updated its "Obtaining service for your Apple products after the warranty expires" support article, moving the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro and the iPhone X from its vintage list to its obsolete list.

Apple explains that once a device is added to the obsolete list, the company will stop providing all hardware repair services, and service providers will no longer be able to order parts for it.

Products may not be classified as obsolete until more than seven years after Apple stops selling them, though the actual classification timing is ultimately determined by Apple.

On the other hand, Apple's vintage list includes products for which repairs are only provided while parts remain available. Apple classifies products as vintage if they have been out of sale for more than five years but less than seven years.

Apple ended major OS support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, making iOS 16 its final major version. The device currently only supports up to iOS 16.7.16. As for the 2018 15-inch MacBook Pro, it is only supported up to macOS Sequoia, and the currently available version for that model is macOS 15.7.7.

For a complete list of Apple's vintage and obsolete products, and the exceptions where repair service can be extended for up to 10 years, please follow the link here.
